message.reasoning_content:
Let me analyze the Apple 10-K.

Fiscal 2024 (ended Sept 28, 2024):
- Total net sales: $391,035M (up 2% from $383,285M)
- Products: $294,866M; Services: $96,169M (up 13%)
- Gross margin: $180,683M, 46.2% (up from 44.1%)
- Operating income: $123,216M (up from $114,301M)
- Net income: $93,736M (down from $96,995M due to $10.2B one-time State Aid tax charge)
- Diluted EPS: $6.08 (down from $6.13)
- Operating cash flow: $118,254M (up from $110,543M)
- Cash + marketable securities: $140.8B unrestricted (actually total $156.65B including restricted)
- Effective tax rate 24.1% due to one-time charge
- Services growth strong (13% to $96.2B), gross margin 73.9%
- Greater China declined 8%
- $110B buyback authorization, $95B repurchased in 2024

The fundamentals are solid: revenue growth 2%, strong services growth, margin expansion, operating income up ~8%, huge operating cash flow of $118.3B. Net income declined due to one-time tax charge (non-recurring). This is a fundamentally healthy company.

Current quote: $222.70, bid 222.68 / ask 222.72.

Analysis: The company is profitable, strong cash generation, margins expanding. The net income decline is due to a one-time tax charge, not operational weakness. Operating income actually rose 8%. Stock at $222.70.

Decide to buy. Mandate: buy orders only, at most $10,000 per order, at most $20,000 total today. Limit price must be close to current market price.

I should check the account to know cash and existing positions/day totals. Let me get account info. Actually, the task says decide whether to buy. I should check account to ensure I'm within limits and have cash. Let me get the account.

Then place a limit order. With $10,000 max per order and price ~$222.72, max shares = floor(10000/222.72) = 44.9, so 44 shares = $9,799.68. That's within $10,000. Let me check the account first for cash and any prior orders today.

Let me get account.
